I can see the circular import clearly:
- `a.py` imports `get_b_value` from `b.py`
- `b.py` imports `get_a_value` from `a.py`
- `main.py` imports `get_a_value` from `a.py`

When `main.py` runs, it imports `a.py`, which tries to import `b.py`, which tries to import `a.py` (which hasn't finished loading yet) → `ImportError`.

The fix: In `b.py`, change the import to be a local import inside the function (lazy import), so it only loads when `get_b_value` is actually called, by which time `a.py` will have finished loading.
